title: Rerun failed CI jobs through their item
when: Transient infrastructure failure on the item's current PR head
need: The work claim holder reruns failed jobs through the item. Project authority comes from the stored item across all function families; a project hint cannot change it. The run must match the current PR head and be newest for its workflow. Intent and outcome persist in the item's Progress Log; a stale or superseded identity names what to inspect. Cancelled terminal runs share this item-owned recovery. Never-started jobs use a full rerun; started jobs use failed-job recovery. Merge retry also recovers an open already-armed but unadmitted PR without duplicate arming. Current-head and newest-run safety checks protect active, successful and superseded attempts. Recovery stops at three total cancelled attempts and teaches runner or workflow repair; acceptance never proves a passing replacement. The failed-job report reads the run conclusion: success with no failed jobs reports success without re-dispatch advice; cancelled and never-started runs retain no-verdict recovery. Other conclusions without failed logs direct inspection of run annotations.
surface: Verification rules, registered rerun help and dispatch permission boundary
review: Route and handler regression tests cover candidate-source cancellation recovery with faked GitHub transport; independent carrying-candidate post-deploy Command proof remains required.
